blocks.text: System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) is a standard protocol that you can use to provision and manage users and groups. Zscaler provides an easy and consistent mechanism to use SCIM and manage the user and group accounts lifecycle.

blocks.item: Provisioning users and groups onto Zscaler.
Automatically updating a user's group and department in the Zscaler user database to align with the changes in your user directory.
Deprovisioning users from Zscaler's database when users are deleted from your user directory.

blocks.text: When creating users, the domain included in the username must be preregistered with Authentication Service. For example, if a user has the username "test@zscalerexample.com", the domain "zscalerexample.com" needs to be registered with your tenant on Authentication Service.

Authentication Service classifies attributes into two types: system-defined user attributes and custom user attributes. In addition, Zscaler supports default SCIM group attributes and standard SCIM operations.
The following table provides information on the association between system-defined user attributes and the corresponding UI label name in Authentication Service.

table: The display name of the user. This is a mandatory attribute.
The first name of the user
The last name of the user
The middle name of the user
The user's primary email address. This is a mandatory attribute.
The user's status confirming whether the user is enabled or disabled
The user's preferred language of communication
The department to which the user belongs
The user ID of the manager
The cost center to which the user belongs
The division to which the user belongs
The formatted name of the user
The organization to which the user belongs
The user ID used for authentication
The type of the user such as employee or customer
The timezone to which the user belongs

blocks.text: The following table provides information on the association between the default system-defined user attributes and the corresponding name in Authentication Service.

table: The unique identifier assigned to the user
The client-assigned identifier for the user which is unique within the client's context
The timestamp indicating when the user resource was created
The timestamp indicating the last modification to the user resource
The URI representing the location of the user resource in the SCIM server
The version of the user resource. The version is updated with every modification to the user resource
The type indicating the resource type. In this case, the resource type should be User.
A list of group memberships of the user. These groups allow access control and association.

blocks.text: The following table provides a list of custom user attributes and their corresponding SCIM mappings.

table: A string representing the user's title or honorific, such as Mr., Ms., Dr., etc.
A string representing the suffix of a person's name, such as Jr., Sr., III, etc.
The URL pointing to the user's profile page
The string indicating the user's locale, typically used for language and regional settings (e.g., en-US)
The instant messaging addresses associated with the user
The URLs pointing to the user's photos or avatars
The set of entitlements granted to the user, such as access roles or permissions
The list of roles assigned to the user (e.g., admin, manager)
X.509 public key certificates associated with the user
A unique identifier assigned to the employee, typically used within an enterprise

blocks.text: The following table provides information on the association between SCIM group attributes and the corresponding column name in Authentication Service.

table: The unique ID generated by Zscaler
The external ID provided by the client and stored in the Zscaler's database
The timestamp when the group was created
The timestamp when the group was last updated
The URL to locate the group resource
The version of the group resource. The version is updated for each modification to the group resource.
The type indicating the resource type. In this case, the resource type should be Group.
The display name of the group
The list of users or resources associated with the group
